note: This is a modelled upper-bound reference, not a loss forecast, not a fine estimate and not legal advice. It answers one question only: if every unmet obligation in scope were enforced at its statutory ceiling, what order of magnitude is on the table. Voluntary frameworks carry no ceiling, which is deliberate - it separates gaps with statutory teeth from gaps that are posture only.
method: For each system, for each penalty class engaged, exposure = ceiling x unmet share of that class's applicable requirements, where unmet share is 1 minus the evidence coverage of the controls satisfying them. Summed across systems.

penalty_classes.label: Prohibited practice
penalty_classes.cite: AI Act Art. 99(3) - up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher

penalty_classes.label: High-risk and operator obligations
penalty_classes.cite: AI Act Art. 99(4) - up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher

penalty_classes.label: Data subject rights and processing principles
penalty_classes.cite: GDPR Art. 83(5) - up to EUR 20 000 000 or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher

penalty_classes.label: Controller and processor obligations
penalty_classes.cite: GDPR Art. 83(4) - up to EUR 10 000 000 or 2% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher

penalty_classes.label: Voluntary framework - no statutory penalty
penalty_classes.cite: ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI RMF are voluntary. Gaps here carry assurance, contractual and certification consequences, not administrative fines.
